items: Iterable: any object that can produce an iterator.
It implements `__iter__()` and nothing more.
Iterator: the object that actually produces values.
It implements both `__iter__()` and `__next__()`.
Every iterator is iterable — its `__iter__` returns self.

blocks.text: The reverse is false. Most iterables are not iterators.

items: Iterables are reusable: fresh iterator per `for`.
Iterators are single-use and exhaust permanently.
One list, many independent cursors over it.
list, tuple, dict, set, str.
range, file objects, `collections.deque`.

blocks.title: Book & Bookmark
blocks.text: Iterable = the book. Iterator = the bookmark. One book holds many bookmarks; each bookmark walks forward once.

items: `iter(obj)` calls `type(obj).__iter__(obj)`.
Looked up on the *type*, so `__getattr__` is bypassed.

`StopIteration` is control flow, not an error.

items: An exhausted iterator raises `StopIteration` forever.
It must never resurrect — the closing invariant.
PEP 234 shipped this protocol in Python 2.2.
Every loop construct in the language rests on it.
Unpacking: `a, b = pair`.
`list()`, `sum()`, the `in` operator.
`*args` splatting and every comprehension.
`__iter__` returns self; `__next__` advances state.
State lives in instance attributes.

blocks.title: Identical Behaviour
blocks.text: Twelve lines of class and three lines of generator produce the same values. Pick the class only when you need the object, not the loop.

items: Any `yield` in the body makes it a generator function.
Calling it runs NO code at all.
It returns a generator object instead.
That object is already an iterator, for free.
`yield` suspends the frame and hands out a value.
All locals and the instruction pointer survive.
`next()` resumes right after the yield expression.
Falling off the end raises `StopIteration` for you.
`return value` sets `StopIteration.value`.
Read it via `yield from` or by catching the exception.
Many yields in one body.
Yields inside `while` and `for` loops.
Yields inside `try/finally` blocks.

blocks.title: Resumable Function
blocks.text: A generator is cooperative multitasking in miniature, not a data structure. `return` destroys the frame; `yield` freezes it on the heap for later.

items: The frame is heap-allocated, kept alive by the generator.
That is why locals survive suspension.
`CO_GENERATOR` on the code object triggers all this.
`gi_frame.f_locals` shows a paused generator's variables.
`g.close()` throws `GeneratorExit` at the pause point.
The generator must not yield again after it.
`try/finally` and `with` run cleanup on close or GC.
Reference cycles round a paused frame delay cleanup.
Never trust GC timing to release a file handle.
A value is produced only when it is requested.
Work is deferred, and possibly never done at all.
One frame plus one item: O(1) space, any length.

blocks.title: Bites In Production
items: Un-primed `send()` raises TypeError — advance once first.
`RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`.
Mutating a list while iterating silently skips elements.
A generator object is always truthy — `if g:` tests nothing.
An abandoned generator can hold a file open forever.
Use `with` inside the generator, or `contextlib.closing`.
`return x` does NOT yield x — it ends the generator.
x is hidden in `StopIteration.value` instead.
A paused generator has no visible stack in a traceback.
Errors appear at the consumption site, not the definition.
List comp: indexable, `len` works — small/medium reused data.
Genexp: no index, no `len` — single pass over large data.
`range`: integers only, ideal for numeric loop bounds.

blocks.text: Generator functions also get try/finally cleanup. Iterator classes get introspection and picklability.

caption.text: Most Python devs write `yield` for years without ever seeing what it actually does: it freezes a stack frame on the heap and hands the caller a bookmark. This handbook walks the whole iteration model — iter/next mechanics, hand-rolled iterator classes, generator internals (gi_frame, GeneratorExit, PEP 479), lazy pipelines, itertools, and the silent-zero bugs that only show up in production. Save it for the next time `sum(g)` returns 0 and nothing raises.
